input.rationale: Keeping candidate 0a6d446a083a42cf91e99726f577eaea active at the end of the available run time, with its remaining discriminator retained rather than resolved by assertion. Current state of the investigation: the obligation claim-config-publish-requires-durable-append is a confirmed implementation violation through direct check 3b256fe6f42b4154b75d4d2ec02e27bf (execution 452a068dbfa1488ea15bc730a0f1e7bd, checker correspondence no_issue_found, outcome violated), where a leader that received a LogStore.StoreLogs error for a membership-change entry still published the configuration as configurations.latest even though the assigned log index was absent from durable storage, and where the node then could not regain leadership because its live quorum counted the unreachable voter. Exploration 6c1f4fbd37ad49e79cd922b03259d1fe added the follower-side negative result: with every StoreLogs call failing on a follower of a real two-node replication path, the follower neither published the configuration nor advanced its cached last-log index. Exploration b1b1d3fba8164059b25bbefb147d3fdb answered the truncation timing conditionally: after a conflicting suffix was deleted and the replacement write failed, durable_last_index fell to 1 while the cached and reported last index stayed 4 with the entry absent from the store. The one open unknown is therefore exactly the boundary that needs a successor: whether that conflicting-suffix-then-failed-write history can be produced by real producers, that is by a second leader elected in a higher term, instead of by supplying the conflicting AppendEntries directly to the handler. That successor would need a multi-node cluster in which one node accumulates uncommitted entries while isolated, a different leader is elected and appends at those indices, and the isolated node's store fails only during the replication that overwrites the suffix. Keeping the candidate active preserves the confirmed finding, the negative result, the conditional truncation evidence, and the stated boundary together, so the remaining work is visible and no result is overstated at run end.

question_candidates.stop_reason: Sourced contract violation in the membership/authority transition path. configurations.latest is documented as the latest configuration in the log/snapshot (configuration.go:254-265) and is the sole authority input for the leader's quorum: quorumSize() (raft.go:1086-1094) counts voters from r.configurations.latest, and commitment.setConfiguration (commitment.go:53-64) rebuilds the match-index voter set from the new configuration. appendConfigurationEntry (raft.go:1203-1240) must therefore only install a configuration that exists in the log, but it calls dispatchLogs first and then unconditionally runs setLatestConfiguration / commitment.setConfiguration / startStopReplication. dispatchLogs (raft.go:1244-1283) assigns applyLog.log.Index before StoreLogs and returns after responding the error, so future.Index() is still nonzero when the write failed. A retained clean-copy execution (exploration 19c98425e4d9482cadcf9bfa3e4f7a85) supplied one transient LogStore.StoreLogs failure on a single-voter cluster that had committed index 3 and observed: AddVoter returned the store error; the assigned index 4 is absent from durable storage (durable last index 3, raft last index 3); the published configuration lists a phantom second voter; and the node then never regains leadership over 142 samples (state Candidate, quorum 2, reachable voters 1), i.e. progress stops until restart. This claim is the sourced requirement, not the experiment; the harness and events are retained with the exploration.

selections.rationale: Sourced suspicion: appendConfigurationEntry (raft.go:1203-1241) calls dispatchLogs first, then unconditionally executes r.setLatestConfiguration(configuration, index), r.leaderState.commitment.setConfiguration(configuration) and r.startStopReplication(). dispatchLogs (raft.go:1244-1279) assigns applyLog.log.Index before StoreLogs and returns early only on its own error path, so future.Index() is still nonzero and the new configuration is published even though nothing was durably stored. The live configuration is the authority input for quorumSize()/checkLeaderLease() (raft.go:1036-1101), requestVote/requestPreVote admission (raft.go:1603-1813) and the election-start gate in runFollower (raft.go:158-260), so publishing an unpersisted configuration can change the node's own quorum requirement. The harness supplies a transient LogStore.StoreLogs failure at the real boundary (storage failure injection) on an otherwise healthy single-voter cluster that had just committed index 3. Observed (CA_EVENT config_publish_after_failed_durable_write): AddVoter returned the store error; the assigned log index 4 is absent from durable storage (getlog_at_assigned_idx_err=log not found, durable_last_index_after=3, raft_last_index=3); yet the node's published configuration now lists two voters (the real one plus phantom/phantom-addr). Observed (CA_EVENT progress_after_failed_durable_write): after the failure the node never regains leadership over 141 samples/1.5s (state=Candidate, ever_leader_in_window=false) because voters_in_live_configuration=2 sets quorum_size_live=2 while only 1 voter is reachable, so electSelf/preElectSelf can never reach the needed tally. This is conditional evidence: it establishes what the fixed code did for an explicitly supplied transient storage failure; the failure itself is injected, not produced by real producers here. A separate observation from the same run: Raft.GetConfiguration().Index() (api.go:897-906 building configurations{latest:...} without latestIndex, returned by configurationsFuture.Index() in future.go:267-270) reports 0 for this two-voter configuration (config_index_after=0), so the published index of the live authority context is not observable and cannot be used as the prevIndex guard that AddVoter/RemoveServer accept. Unresolved discriminators: whether an equivalent divergence is reachable without storage failure; whether a restart (durable log lacks the entry) is the only recovery path; and the exact set of store-failure timings (pre- vs post-StoreLogs) that produce the divergence.

This exploration reduces the two recorded gaps for candidate 0a6d446a083a42cf91e99726f577eaea. Gap 2 (recovery path), closed by a new in-package Go test run: after a transient LogStore.StoreLogs failure made AddVoter(phantom) install a two-voter latest while the durable log still ends at index 2, the node was shut down and a fresh Raft was constructed from the same durable store and snapshot store. Observed (CA_EVENT restart_after_failed_durable_write): servers_before_restart lists the real voter plus phantom/phantom-addr/Voter, while servers_after_restart lists exactly one voter and became_leader_after=true (commit index 3). So the durable log, not the published configuration, is the recovered truth, and a restart is a working recovery path. The same run also bounded the running-process behaviour: after the failed change the node stayed Candidate with ever_leader_in_window=false over 141 samples because quorum_size_live=2 equals one unreachable voter plus itself (CA_EVENT progress_after_failed_durable_write); source reasoning explains the absence of self-repair, since the only running paths that revert r.configurations.latest to the committed value are the appendEntries truncation branch (raft.go:1530) and installSnapshot (raft.go:1937), and both require a leader while no leader can be elected against an unreachable voter. Gap 1 (no-error reachability), answered as a sourced negative result plus a success-path control: the success control CA_EVENT config_persist_success_control shows AddVoter error <nil>, getlog_at_assigned_idx_err <nil> for the assigned index 4 and durable_last_index_after=4, i.e. the published two-voter configuration has a durable counterpart; that fixes the comparing value (the divergence does not appear when the write succeeds). Enumerating every publishing site shows appendConfigurationEntry (raft.go:1203-1240 -> raft.go:1237) is the only site that can install a configuration absent from the log: appendEntries truncation reverts to the committed configuration (raft.go:1530), processConfigurationLogEntry installs the configuration of an entry that was just stored or read from the log (raft.go:1588-1598), installSnapshot installs the received snapshot's configuration (raft.go:1937), and startup restore installs the snapshot's configuration (api.go:664). No no-error route to the divergence was found. Retained evidence for this exploration is the clean-copy execution the controller associates with the submitted harness; the failure is injected at the real LogStore boundary (explicitly supplied precondition, not produced by real producers), and the phantom voter's unreachability is supplied by the harness's lack of a route to phantom-addr.

Formal direct check of the accepted unit unit-claim-config-publish-requires-durable-append for obligation claim-config-publish-requires-durable-append. The obligation requires that a configuration installed as configurations.latest must have its entry in the durable log. The plan admits one leader-established operation (assurance_leader_established with alias adm) and one membership-change attempt (assurance_config_change_attempt with alias act), then inspects the result event assurance_config_published emitted for that same operation (identity field node). The property asserts entry_durable is true whenever the configuration was published ahead of a durable entry (trigger published_ahead_of_durable true). The harness bootstraps one voter over an InmemStore whose StoreLogs can be failed on demand at the real LogStore boundary, waits for leadership, emits the two prerequisites, runs AddVoter while exactly one StoreLogs call fails, then reports whether the log index assigned to that change is present in the store; previous clean-copy runs of the same harness observed add_voter_error set, assigned index 4 absent from the store, and the published configuration listing a second voter. Only one failing StoreLogs timing is exercised here, and the failure is an explicitly supplied fault rather than a producer-generated condition; both are recorded as plan uncertainties. The plan and harness are submitted as separate draft files; plan.harness.source and files are intentionally omitted so the controller fixes the harness bytes.

feedback.answered: Two recorded unknowns are answered by executed evidence, not by argument. First, the exact recovery path: exploration check cb2a8bf5289046f9a58098b950a38762 recorded restart_after_failed_durable_write, where a node whose published configuration listed the extra voter phantom/phantom-addr/Voter was shut down and rebuilt with NewRaft over the same durable store and snapshot store; after the restart servers_after_restart lists exactly one voter and became_leader_after is true, so the durable log is the recovered truth and a restart is a working recovery path. The same execution also bounds the running process: progress_after_failed_durable_write shows state Candidate with ever_leader_in_window false over 141 samples because the live quorum counts the unreachable voter, and the only running paths that revert latest to the committed value (appendEntries truncation and installSnapshot) require a leader, so nothing in the running process repairs the authority context. Second, whether the divergence is reachable without a LogStore error: the same execution includes the success-path control config_persist_success_control, where AddVoter returns nil, the assigned log index is present in the store and durable_last_index_after matches it, so the published configuration has a durable counterpart whenever the write succeeds; enumerating every setLatestConfiguration call site shows appendConfigurationEntry is the only site that can install a configuration absent from the log, while truncation reverts to the committed configuration and processConfigurationLogEntry and installSnapshot install configurations taken from stored entries or a received snapshot. No no-error route was found.

selections.rationale: This exploration tests the follower half of the narrowed discriminator on candidate 0a6d446a083a42cf91e99726f577eaea and leaves the leader-side result (confirmed direct check 3b256fe6f42b4154b75d4d2ec02e27bf, execution 452a068dbfa1488ea15bc730a0f1e7bd) untouched. Method: two in-process nodes are bootstrapped with both addresses as voters, their InmemTransports are connected to each other, both Rafts are started, one node is detected as leader, and the follower's LogStore wrapper is set to fail every StoreLogs call while the leader runs a real AddVoter. Observed (CA_EVENT follower_store_failure): the failing follower attempted 8 store writes and all 8 failed (store_log_attempts 8, store_log_failures 8), yet follower_published_phantom is false, follower_servers_after equals follower_servers_before, follower_durable_before and follower_durable_after are both 2 and follower_last_index is 2. That is a bounded negative result for this path, and it matches the source: appendEntries stores the new entries and only then calls processConfigurationLogEntry, so a StoreLogs error returns before any configuration is published and before setLastLog advances the cached last index (src-follower-gate material covers the corresponding runFollower gate; the store call order is in the appendEntries tail of the same test harness reading). Boundaries and what is NOT decided here: this run does not exercise a failure that occurs after a log truncation has already deleted a conflicting suffix, where the same appendEntries path returns before setLastLog and the cached last-log can then be higher than the store content, which is the timing this discriminator still lists; that remainder is a sourced hypothesis, not an observation. The fault is still injected at the real LogStore boundary, and the two-node cluster is in-memory. Reusing the same harness keeps the earlier leader-side events available in the same clean-copy execution, so this submission adds the follower probe without weakening the retained confirmation.

feedback.answered: The follower half of the discriminator is settled by executed evidence. Exploration check 6c1f4fbd37ad49e79cd922b03259d1fe built a two-node in-process cluster with both addresses as voters and their InmemTransports connected, then failed every StoreLogs call on the detected follower while the leader ran a real AddVoter. So a follower-side durable failure does not publish the configuration or advance the follower's cached last-log index: appendEntries stores new entries and only reaches processConfigurationLogEntry after a successful StoreLogs, so the failure returns first. selections.rationale: Conditional probe of the last open timing. Method: one bootstrapped voter is driven through real calls (leader election, then two Apply calls) so its log holds indices 1 to 4 with index 1 the configuration entry and term T for 2 to 4; the harness then delivers one AppendEntries for a different leader in term T+5 whose PrevLogEntry is 1 with matching term and whose entries conflict at indices 2, 3 and 4, while the node's LogStore wrapper fails every StoreLogs call. This is a direct handler invocation (r.appendEntries), so it bypasses the transport, checkRPCHeader and main-loop serialization, and the peer leader identity and higher term are supplied rather than produced by an election; the handler, the log store, the truncation path and the terms are the fixed target code. Observed (CA_EVENT truncation_then_store_failure): durable_last_index_before is 4 and durable_last_index_after is 1, because the conflicting suffix was deleted before the write, while cached_last_index_after stays 4, reported_last_index (Raft.LastIndex) is 4, getlog_at_cached_err is log not found, append_success is false and cached_ahead_of_durable is true. So after a truncation whose replacement write fails, the node both caches and reports a last-log index whose entry no longer exists in durable storage, which is exactly the state the in-code TODO at raft.go:1536-1545 describes. This answers the discriminator with a conditional observation on the fixed code and does not by itself establish a full protocol history, since the conflicting AppendEntries was supplied rather than produced; a protocol-level version would need a second leader in a higher term to be elected through real producers. The confirmed leader-side violation (direct check 3b256fe6f42b4154b75d4d2ec02e27bf) and the follower negative result (exploration 6c1f4fbd37ad49e79cd922b03259d1fe) are unchanged.

Sourced contract violation in the membership/authority transition path. configurations.latest is documented as the latest configuration in the log/snapshot (configuration.go:254-265) and is the sole authority input for the leader's quorum: quorumSize() (raft.go:1086-1094) counts voters from r.configurations.latest, and commitment.setConfiguration (commitment.go:53-64) rebuilds the match-index voter set from the new configuration. appendConfigurationEntry (raft.go:1203-1240) must therefore only install a configuration that exists in the log, but it calls dispatchLogs first and then unconditionally runs setLatestConfiguration / commitment.setConfiguration / startStopReplication. dispatchLogs (raft.go:1244-1283) assigns applyLog.log.Index before StoreLogs and returns after responding the error, so future.Index() is still nonzero when the write failed. A retained clean-copy execution (exploration 19c98425e4d9482cadcf9bfa3e4f7a85) supplied one transient LogStore.StoreLogs failure on a single-voter cluster that had committed index 3 and observed: AddVoter returned the store error; the assigned index 4 is absent from durable storage (durable last index 3, raft last index 3); the published configuration lists a phantom second voter; and the node then never regains leadership over 142 samples (state Candidate, quorum 2, reachable voters 1), i.e. progress stops until restart. This claim is the sourced requirement, not the experiment; the harness and events are retained with the exploration.

The same run also bounded the running-process behaviour: after the failed change the node stayed Candidate with ever_leader_in_window=false over 141 samples because quorum_size_live=2 equals one unreachable voter plus itself (CA_EVENT progress_after_failed_durable_write); source reasoning explains the absence of self-repair, since the only running paths that revert r.configurations.latest to the committed value are the appendEntries truncation branch (raft.go:1530) and installSnapshot (raft.go:1937), and both require a leader while no leader can be elected against an unreachable voter. Gap 1 (no-error reachability), answered as a sourced negative result plus a success-path control: the success control CA_EVENT config_persist_success_control shows AddVoter error <nil>, getlog_at_assigned_idx_err <nil> for the assigned index 4 and durable_last_index_after=4, i.e. the published two-voter configuration has a durable counterpart; that fixes the comparing value (the divergence does not appear when the write succeeds). Enumerating every publishing site shows appendConfigurationEntry (raft.go:1203-1240 -> raft.go:1237) is the only site that can install a configuration absent from the log: appendEntries truncation reverts to the committed configuration (raft.go:1530), processConfigurationLogEntry installs the configuration of an entry that was just stored or read from the log (raft.go:1588-1598), installSnapshot installs the received snapshot's configuration (raft.go:1937), and startup restore installs the snapshot's configuration (api.go:664). No no-error route to the divergence was found. Retained evidence for this exploration is the clean-copy execution the controller associates with the submitted harness; the failure is injected at the real LogStore boundary (explicitly supplied precondition, not produced by real producers), and the phantom voter's unreachability is supplied by the harness's lack of a route to phantom-addr.

Formal direct check of the accepted unit unit-claim-config-publish-requires-durable-append for obligation claim-config-publish-requires-durable-append. The obligation requires that a configuration installed as configurations.latest must have its entry in the durable log. The plan admits one leader-established operation (assurance_leader_established with alias adm) and one membership-change attempt (assurance_config_change_attempt with alias act), then inspects the result event assurance_config_published emitted for that same operation (identity field node). The property asserts entry_durable is true whenever the configuration was published ahead of a durable entry (trigger published_ahead_of_durable true). Only one failing StoreLogs timing is exercised here, and the failure is an explicitly supplied fault rather than a producer-generated condition; both are recorded as plan uncertainties. Method: one bootstrapped voter is driven through real calls (leader election, then two Apply calls) so its log holds indices 1 to 4 with index 1 the configuration entry and term T for 2 to 4; the harness then delivers one AppendEntries for a different leader in term T+5 whose PrevLogEntry is 1 with matching term and whose entries conflict at indices 2, 3 and 4, while the node's LogStore wrapper fails every StoreLogs call. This is a direct handler invocation (r.appendEntries), so it bypasses the transport, checkRPCHeader and main-loop serialization, and the peer leader identity and higher term are supplied rather than produced by an election; the handler, the log store, the truncation path and the terms are the fixed target code. Observed (CA_EVENT truncation_then_store_failure): durable_last_index_before is 4 and durable_last_index_after is 1, because the conflicting suffix was deleted before the write, while cached_last_index_after stays 4, reported_last_index (Raft.LastIndex) is 4, getlog_at_cached_err is log not found, append_success is false and cached_ahead_of_durable is true. So after a truncation whose replacement write fails, the node both caches and reports a last-log index whose entry no longer exists in durable storage, which is exactly the state the in-code TODO at raft.go:1536-1545 describes. This answers the discriminator with a conditional observation on the fixed code and does not by itself establish a full protocol history, since the conflicting AppendEntries was supplied rather than produced; a protocol-level version would need a second leader in a higher term to be elected through real producers. The confirmed leader-side violation (direct check 3b256fe6f42b4154b75d4d2ec02e27bf) and the follower negative result (exploration 6c1f4fbd37ad49e79cd922b03259d1fe) are unchanged.

selections.rationale: Keeping candidate 0a6d446a083a42cf91e99726f577eaea active at the end of the available run time, with its remaining discriminator retained rather than resolved by assertion. Current state of the investigation: the obligation claim-config-publish-requires-durable-append is a confirmed implementation violation through direct check 3b256fe6f42b4154b75d4d2ec02e27bf (execution 452a068dbfa1488ea15bc730a0f1e7bd, checker correspondence no_issue_found, outcome violated), where a leader that received a LogStore.StoreLogs error for a membership-change entry still published the configuration as configurations.latest even though the assigned log index was absent from durable storage, and where the node then could not regain leadership because its live quorum counted the unreachable voter. Exploration 6c1f4fbd37ad49e79cd922b03259d1fe added the follower-side negative result: with every StoreLogs call failing on a follower of a real two-node replication path, the follower neither published the configuration nor advanced its cached last-log index. The one open unknown is therefore exactly the boundary that needs a successor: whether that conflicting-suffix-then-failed-write history can be produced by real producers, that is by a second leader elected in a higher term, instead of by supplying the conflicting AppendEntries directly to the handler. That successor would need a multi-node cluster in which one node accumulates uncommitted entries while isolated, a different leader is elected and appends at those indices, and the isolated node's store fails only during the replication that overwrites the suffix. Keeping the candidate active preserves the confirmed finding, the negative result, the conditional truncation evidence, and the stated boundary together, so the remaining work is visible and no result is overstated at run end.
